question.text: Certain organic compound on combustion produces three gaseous oxides A, B and C. A and C turned lime water milky, B turned anhydrous <math><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">u</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> blue and C turned <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msub></math> solution green. The elements present in organic compounds are

solution.text:
The elements present in organic compounds are C, H, S and their oxides are CO2,H2O,SO2 respectively.
CO2 turns lime water milky, water turns anhydrous copper sulphate blue and SO2 being reducing agent can reduce K2Cr2O7 into green coloured Cr3+ compound CrCl3 etc.
